findings.text: follow-on: _selene_psrc_loader is private and has no production caller — only tests/eval/test_selene_reference.py reaches it — so the SELENE reference geometry is reduced by nothing but the test until the stamping node wires the loader into read_efit_geometry's loader= argument. The seam itself is complete and firewall-gated.

follow-on (declared by the run): the X-point the loader passes is masked for JT-60SA because build_geometry_from_arrays' shared _null_in_vessel gates on the MAST limiter box XPOINT_VESSEL_R_RANGE=(0.1, 2.0), while calRX for shot 100599 reaches 4.483 m — outside it — so the X-point slot is nulled and GeometryVerdict cannot score it. Verified independently: calRX range 1.705..4.483. A machine-aware in-vessel box would let the X-point comparison run; equilibrium_labels.py is not this node's write path.

follow-on: shot 100599 caches no surfABVxp (verified — /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/100599.zarr/PSRC carries no surfABVxp array), so the loader's boundary reduction has only ever run on the test's synthetic slot, packed with the same layout constants the reader decodes. The packed layout is therefore confirmed by the reader's own assumptions rather than an independent contour; a real SELENE boundary arrives only with the §7 read-only EDDB fetch.

item_verdicts.goal: the node adds §7's jtmm-selene-reference-loader exactly as specified: a private _selene_psrc_loader (imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py:120) reached only through read_efit_geometry(shot_id, frame_times, loader=...), the one read path gated by evaluator_context. It does not read SELENE itself — it calls read_psrc_record (the one SELENE reader) with cache_root/extractor forwarded, and reduces the record through build_geometry_from_arrays, the builder behind the seam's default loader, deriving no geometry of its own. The axis it passes is PSRC's magnetic axis (calRp0/calZp0) interpolated onto the boundary base t_eq; calCCSRc/calCCSZc is never read and the code names that omission. The X-point is passed as a (1, nt) one-null set with time on the last axis and the per-slice boundary contours are NaN-padded to a common (n_bdy, nt) array. Verified independently against the cached shot: at t=0.05 the real axis (2.610, 0.702) differs from the centre (3.200, 0.600) by 0.599 m, so the axis source is a real choice, and the loader's axis test recovers calRp0 to 1e-4.

The declared docs/figures/jt60sa-machine-map/jtmm-selene-reference-loader directory is untouched, correctly, because the done-when names no figure. The reviewed worktree is clean at fac354d9.

justifications.durability: four tests carry meaningful asserts: the axis test both equals calRp0 and differs from the geometric centre, the LCFS test recovers a 0.4 m circle about the axis to 2e-3 across two slices of different vertex counts, the firewall test requires FirewallViolation outside evaluator_context, and judge_geometry scores a geometry against itself at zero boundary RMS. The declared negative control fires. It is weaker where the synthetic boundary is packed with the same layout constants the reader assumes, so a layout error would not be caught by the suite, and where the loader has no production caller yet so nothing but the test drives it.
justifications.evidence: the gate reproduces: gate-selene-loader.log is '15 passed' PYTEST_EXIT=0 at e589f030 and my independent head arm at fac354d9 gives 15 passed EXIT=0 with module.__file__ under the scratch tree (review-head-arm.log). The declared negative control reproduces exactly under my own mutation: swapping the loader's axis source to PSRC's geometric centre calCCSRc/calCCSZc in a scratch tree reddens test_axis_is_psrc_magnetic_axis_not_geometric_centre and (via the mis-centred contour) test_both_slices_resample_to_finite_lcfs_radii, 2 failed and 2 passed, EXIT=1 (review-negative-control-centre-as-axis.log) against a green head arm. Independent real-data checks pass: axis vs centre differ by 0.599 m at t=0.05, calRX reaches 4.483 m, and shot 100599 caches no surfABVxp. Two gaps lower this: the reviewed record's baseline_suite and after_suite are null, so it supplies no base arm (I supplied one), and the boundary reduction is exercised only against a synthetic slot, so the packed layout is confirmed by the reader's own decoder rather than an independent contour.
justifications.fit: the loader follows the module's idiom: a private underscore function, __all__ unchanged, a lazy local numpy import (the module imports numpy locally elsewhere too, at :295), no new public definition, and a docstring that states the mechanism (the axis is PSRC's own; the centre is deliberately unread; the X-point is a one-null set; the boundary is NaN-padded). No version, plan, sprint or ticket identifier appears in any name, comment or docstring.
